sources.title: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in US general election
Pope Leo makes history with US midterm vote

en.title: Pope Leo Casts Mail‑In Vote in U.S. Midterms
en.dek: Pope Leo XIV, the first U.S.-born pontiff, cast a mail‑in ballot in Chicago for the November 3 midterm election.
facts: According to the Vatican press office, Pope Leo XIV cast a mail‑in ballot in Chicago for the November 3 midterm election.
The Vatican said the pope believes in the right and duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes.
The pope has voted in five Illinois primary elections as Robert Prevost, alternating between Democratic and Republican ballots.
The U.S. State Department says it may review the citizenship status of Americans serving as foreign heads of state.
The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops urged Catholics to put faith before politics in a note on the pope’s vote.
body: Pope Leo XIV, the first U.S.-born pontiff, submitted a mail‑in ballot in Chicago for the November 3 midterm election, and the Vatican press office said on Friday that he exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen whenever he was eligible.

The Vatican confirmed that Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, has voted in five Illinois primary elections since 2000, and records from the Illinois State Board of Elections show that he requested Democratic ballots in 2008 and 2010 and Republican ballots in 2012, 2014, and 2016. The state board does not indicate which candidates he supported.

The U.S. State Department says it may actively review the citizenship status of Americans who serve as foreign heads of state, and the department notes that such Americans are not automatically at risk of losing citizenship. The Vatican’s statement about Leo’s vote was issued on October 30, the day before the election. The vote was requested on October 3, ten days before the pope underwent surgery.

The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops urged Catholics to put faith before politics in a note on the pope’s vote, and the conference’s director of public affairs, Chieko Noguchi, said the vote encourages citizens to exercise civic responsibility. The note was issued after the Vatican’s announcement. The conference also called for upholding human dignity and the common good.

U.S. President Donald Trump has clashed with the pope over immigration and the war on Iran. Trump called the pope weak and criticized his stance on immigration, while the pope responded that he is not afraid of the Trump administration and said he would not be deterred from speaking out about the Gospel.
en.context: Pope Leo XIV was born in Chicago and holds U.S. citizenship. He served as a priest and bishop in Peru for over 20 years before becoming pope in May 2025.

problemsFixed: Paragraphs lacked longer sentences with two clauses; repeated sentence openings; paragraph 2 contained an evaluative sentence; paragraph 5 had too many short sentences; missing factual sentences about Vatican statement date and vote request date.
